title: Mission report
noMission: There is no mission to report yet. Start with Level 1.

outcomes.orbit: Your CubeSat is orbiting {dest} and returning data.
outcomes.eccentric: Your CubeSat ended in an eccentric orbit around {dest}.
outcomes.no-fuel: Your CubeSat ran out of propellant before entering orbit around {dest}.

cmlExplain.1: The idea exists, but the design doesn't meet the constraints yet.
cmlExplain.2: The design is feasible, but the mission didn't stay in orbit.
cmlExplain.3: The mission works; there are still trade-offs to improve (orbit or science).
cmlExplain.4: A concrete design that meets its science goals with a good margin.

hintsTitle: How to reach a higher CML

reasons.max: You reached the highest maturity level in the game.
reasons.budget: Your performance earned CML {base}, but the Level 1 budget split capped it at CML {cap}.
reasons.design: The CubeSat doesn't meet every Workshop constraint.
reasons.insertion: The insertion burn didn't leave the CubeSat in orbit.
reasons.eccentric: You're in orbit, but it's eccentric: data arrives with gaps.
reasons.science: The orbit is stable, but the science isn't enough for a point design.

hints.max: Try a harder destination or get more science with less budget.
hints.budget: Go back to Level 1 and pick cards without oversizing or going over budget (maturity {maturity}/100, −{penalty} pts).
hints.flyby: Not enough braking: hold the insertion burn longer or carry more propellant.
hints.crash: Too much braking: release the burn before exceeding the required Δv.
hints.eccentric: Fine-tune the burn: a stable orbit needs 95% to 110% of the required Δv.
hints.instruments: Add another instrument: each one adds science, though a bit less every time.
hints.ground: Invest more in the Ground segment (up to ${full}M): more antennas = more data received.
hints.user: Invest more in the User segment (up to ${full}M): processed, archived data gets used better.
hints.events: During the cruise you lost {lost} science points to events: choose carefully.
hints.general: Aim for a science score of {min} or more with a stable orbit.
hints.noFuel: You ran out of propellant: lighten the spacecraft (less dry mass), carry more propellant or use higher-Isp propulsion.

noInstruments: Your CubeSat carried no instruments, so there is no science data.
flybyData: Flyby: there were only a few minutes of observation, so data is sparse.
noFuelData: With no propellant to brake, the CubeSat flew past: it only took a few measurements on the way.
crashData: The CubeSat was lost before sending data.
chartLabel: {instrument} chart: {title}. {points} simulated measurements compared with a conceptual NASA reference.
simulatedNote: Simulated data for educational purposes. Reference curves are a conceptual comparison with real NASA missions, not their original data. Lower science score = more noise.
learn: Every extra kilogram demands more propellant (rocket equation), solar power falls with the square of distance, and the Ground and User budgets decide how much science actually reaches scientists.
